words.ex_cn: 攀爬是他最喜欢的户外活动。
words.en: Climbing is the activity of climbing up something, especially mountains or rocks, often as a sport or hobby.

words.tr: phrase. 表现出上升趋势；呈上涨态势
words.ex: The number of people using bikes shows an upward trend.
words.ex_cn: 使用自行车的人数呈上升趋势。
words.en: To display or indicate a pattern of increase over time.

words.tr: phrase. 上升趋势；增长趋势
words.ex: The temperature shows an upward trend this week.
words.ex_cn: 这周气温呈上升趋势。
words.en: A general tendency for something to increase or rise over time.

words.tr:
adv. 向上地；
adj. 向上的；
words.ex: The balloon moved upward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 气球缓慢地向上移动。
words.en: Moving or directed toward a higher place or level.

words.tr:
v. 落下；掉下；
n. 滴；下落；
words.ex: The apple dropped from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上落了下来。
words.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

words.tr: v. 掉下；“drop”的现在分词；
words.ex: He was dropping his keys on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把钥匙掉在地板上。
words.en: The act of falling or being allowed to fall vertically; the act of delivering something by parachute.

words.tr:
v. 下降；跌倒；
n. 落下；跌落；秋天；
words.ex: The temperature falls quickly at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚温度迅速下降。
words.en: To move downward, typically rapidly and freely without control, from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr: v. 下降；跌倒；“fall”的现在分词； adj. 衰退的；落下的；跌落的； n. 下降；
words.ex: The temperature is falling quickly.
words.ex_cn: 温度正在迅速下降。
words.en: Moving downward from a higher to a lower level, typically rapidly and without control.

words.tr: phrase. 表现出下降趋势；呈下滑态势
words.ex: The temperature shows a downward trend this week.
words.ex_cn: 这周气温呈下降趋势。
words.en: To display a pattern of decrease over time.

words.tr: phrase. 一种下降的趋势；指某事物在一段时间内持续减少或降低的走向
words.ex: The number of students is showing a downward trend.
words.ex_cn: 学生人数正在呈现下降趋势。
words.en: A gradual decline in value, quantity, or level over a period of time.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: v. 下降；衰退；“decline”的现在分词； adj. 衰退的；下滑的；
words.ex: The number of students is declining each year.
words.ex_cn: 学生人数每年都在下降。
words.en: If something is declining, it is becoming less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: v. 垂直落下；暴跌；
words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.tr: adv. 极大地；值得注目地；
words.ex: The new policy significantly improved student performance.
words.ex_cn: 新政策极大地改善了学生的成绩。
words.en: In a way that is large or important enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.tr: adv. 急剧地；引人注目地；
words.ex: The temperature dropped dramatically overnight.
words.ex_cn: 夜间温度急剧下降。
words.en: In a way that is sudden, noticeable, or significant, often in a way that is intended to produce a strong effect.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；引人注目的；戏剧（性）的；
words.ex: There was a dramatic increase in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度急剧上升。
words.en: If something is dramatic, it happens or changes suddenly and noticeably.

words.tr: adv. 显著地；
words.ex: The results changed markedly after the new method was used.
words.ex_cn: 使用新方法后，结果显著地改变了。
words.en: In a way that is clearly noticeable or significant.

words.tr: v. （使）留痕迹；做标记；评分；“mark”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 明显的；显著的；有记号的；
words.ex: The storm marked the old tree with deep scratches.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在那棵老树上留下了深深的划痕。
words.en: A marked change or difference is very obvious and easily noticed.

words.tr: adv. 显著地；非常地；
words.ex: He performed remarkably well in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中表现得非常出色。
words.en: In a way that is worthy of attention; strikingly.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.tr: adv. 实质上；大体上；
words.ex: The new policy substantially improved the results.
words.ex_cn: 新政策实质上改善了结果。
words.en: To a great extent or degree; considerably.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: adv. 大幅度地；
words.ex: The new policy drastically reduced costs.
words.ex_cn: 新政策大幅度降低了成本。
words.en: In a way that is likely to have a strong or far-reaching effect.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；激烈的；
words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.tr: adv. 大坡度地；
words.ex: The road rises steeply up the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这条路大坡度地向上延伸到山上。
words.en: In a manner that is steep; sharply or abruptly.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr: adv. 急剧地；
words.ex: The price rose sharply last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月价格急剧上涨。
words.en: In a sharp manner; with a sharp edge or point; abruptly; severely.

words.tr: adj. 锋利的；骤变的；灵敏的；尖刻的；
words.ex: The knife is sharp enough to cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀足够锋利，可以切纸。
words.en: Having a thin edge or a fine point that is capable of cutting or piercing; keen.

words.tr: adv. 突然；猛然；骤然；
words.ex: Suddenly, the light went out.
words.ex_cn: 突然，灯灭了。
words.en: If something happens suddenly, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.

words.tr: adj. 突然的；忽然的；
words.ex: There was a sudden noise in the night.
words.ex_cn: 夜里突然传来一阵响声。
words.en: If something is sudden, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.

words.tr: adv. 迅速地；快速地；
words.ex: The car moved rapidly down the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车迅速地沿着道路行驶。
words.en: If something happens rapidly, it happens very quickly.

words.tr: adj. 迅速的
words.ex: The car moved at a rapid speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车以迅速的速度行驶。
words.en: A rapid change or event happens very quickly.

words.tr: adv. 稍微；略微；瘦小地；
words.ex: The room is slightly warmer than before.
words.ex_cn: 房间比以前稍微暖和一点。
words.en: To a small degree; not considerably.

words.tr: adj. 轻微的；微小的；
words.ex: He has a slight cold.
words.ex_cn: 他有点轻微的感冒。
words.en: A slight change, difference, or action is not very great or important.

words.tr: adv. 略微；
words.ex: The temperature rose marginally yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度略微上升了。
words.en: To a very small extent; slightly.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.tr: adv. 渐渐地；逐步地；
words.ex: He gradually learned to ride a bike.
words.ex_cn: 他渐渐学会了骑自行车。
words.en: If something changes or is done gradually, it changes or is done in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 逐渐的；逐步的；渐进的；
words.ex: The change was gradual.
words.ex_cn: 这种变化是逐渐的。
words.en: A gradual change or process happens in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

words.tr: adv. 温柔地；温和地；轻轻地；
words.ex: She gently woke the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她温柔地叫醒了宝宝。
words.en: In a mild, kind, or tender manner; not harshly or severely.

words.tr: adj. 温和的；文雅的；温柔的；
words.ex: The mother gave a gentle hug to her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲给了孩子一个温和的拥抱。
words.en: Someone who is gentle is kind and calm, and does not behave in a violent or harsh way.

words.tr: adv. 适度地；不过分地；有节制地；
words.ex: He eats moderately to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他适度饮食以保持健康。
words.en: In a manner that is neither too much nor too little; to a moderate extent.

words.tr: adj. 适度的；温和的；
words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.tr: adv. 稳定地；
words.ex: The temperature rose steadily throughout the day.
words.ex_cn: 白天温度稳定地上升。
words.en: If something happens or changes steadily, it happens or changes in a regular way without interruption.

words.tr:
adj. 稳定的；
v. 使稳住；
words.ex: The boat moved in a steady way on the calm sea.
words.ex_cn: 船在平静的海面上平稳地移动。
words.en: If something is steady, it is firm and does not shake or move about. If you steady something, you stop it from shaking or moving about.

words.tr: adv. 谦虚地；谨慎地；适度地
words.ex: She modestly accepted the award.
words.ex_cn: 她谦虚地接受了奖项。
words.en: In a way that is not excessive or extreme; with modesty.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: v. 波动；起伏不定；
words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr: n. 波动；起伏；
words.ex: The stock market shows daily fluctuation.
words.ex_cn: 股票市场每天都有波动。
words.en: A fluctuation is a change in something, especially in a continuous process such as temperature, prices, or levels of activity.

words.tr: phrase. 保持稳定；维持不变
words.ex: The price of milk will remain stable this month.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶的价格这个月将保持稳定。
words.en: To continue to be in a particular state or condition without changing.

words.tr: phrase. 保持不变；持续恒定
words.ex: The temperature remains constant during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 在实验过程中，温度保持不变。
words.en: To stay the same and not change.

words.tr: phrase. 保持稳定；保持平稳；保持坚定
words.ex: The price of bread will remain steady this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月面包的价格将保持稳定。
words.en: To continue to be in a particular state or condition without changing.

words.tr: phrase. 保持不变；维持原状；依然未变
words.ex: The price will remain unchanged next month.
words.ex_cn: 价格下个月将保持不变。
words.en: To stay the same; not to change.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.tr:
v. 停留；保持；
n. 停留；逗留；
words.ex: He will stay at home tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚会待在家里。
words.en: To stay means to continue to be in a particular place or situation, or to remain in a specified state or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 达到顶峰；在……达到最高点
words.ex: The temperature peaked at 35 degrees yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度最高达到35摄氏度。
words.en: To reach the highest point or level.

words.tr: phrase. 在……达到最高点；在……达到顶峰
words.ex: The temperature reached the highest point at noon.
words.ex_cn: 温度在中午达到了最高点。
words.en: Attained the maximum level or value at a specific point in time.

words.tr: phrase. 在……达到顶峰；在……达到最高点
words.ex: The temperature reached the peak at noon.
words.ex_cn: 温度在中午达到了峰值。
words.en: Attained the highest level or point of development at a specific time.

words.tr: phrase. 在……处到达底部；触底于
words.ex: He reached the bottom at the end of the slide.
words.ex_cn: 他在滑梯末端到达了底部。
words.en: Attained the lowest level or value at a specific point in time.

words.tr: phrase. 在……时跌至最低点；在……处达到最低水平
words.ex: The temperature reached the lowest point at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 气温在午夜达到最低点。
words.en: Attained the minimum level or point of development at a specific time.

words.tr: adv. 大约；大概；
words.ex: The trip takes approximately 30 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这段旅程大约需要30分钟。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact.

words.tr: adv. 大约；粗略地；
words.ex: There are roughly 100 students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级大约有100名学生。
words.en: In a manner that is not exact or detailed; approximately.

words.tr: adv. 几乎；将近；
words.ex: I nearly missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上差点没赶上公交车。
words.en: Almost, but not quite; very close to.

words.tr: adv. 几乎；
words.ex: He almost finished his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎完成了作业。
words.en: You use almost to indicate that something is not completely the case but is nearly the case.

words.tr:
prep. 在…周围；环绕；
adv. 大约；到处；在附近；环绕；
words.ex: The children are running around the tree.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树周围跑。
words.en: In a position or direction surrounding, or in the vicinity of, a particular place or thing.

words.tr:
prep. 关于；大约；大概；涉及；
adv. 大约；到处；
words.ex: The book is about animals.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于动物的。
words.en: If you talk about something, you are discussing it or mentioning it. If you do something about a problem, you take action to solve it.

words.tr: v. 赶上；超过
words.ex: He will overtake the car ahead soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会超过前面的车。
words.en: If you overtake someone, you go past them because you are moving faster than they are.

words.tr: v. 超过；
words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr: v. 超过；
words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.tr: v. 代替；取代；
words.ex: He will replace the broken chair.
words.ex_cn: 他将代替这把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second.

words.tr: phrase. 代替
words.ex: Computers can take the place of typewriters.
words.ex_cn: 计算机可以取代打字机。
words.en: To take the place of something or someone means to replace them or to be used instead of them.

words.tr: n. 百分比；百分率；
words.ex: The percentage of students who passed the test was 85.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生百分比是85。
words.en: A percentage is a proportion or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.

words.tr: n. 比例；份额；
words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.tr: phrase. 是…的原因；解释；负责；（数量或比例上）占
words.ex: The rain can account for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 下雨是延误的原因。
words.en: If a particular thing accounts for a part or proportion of something, that part or proportion consists of that thing, or is used or produced by it.

words.tr: v. 分配；
words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 分发；分配；
words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.tr: v. 支配；
words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.tr: v. 给…排出先后顺序；给…优先权；
words.ex: We need to prioritise the most urgent tasks.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要给最紧急的任务排出先后顺序。
words.en: If you prioritize something, you treat it as more important than other things.

words.tr: adv. 主要地；
words.ex: The city is predominantly populated by young people.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市主要由年轻人居住。
words.en: If something is predominantly true, it is true to a much greater extent than it is false.

words.tr: adv. 压倒性地；
words.ex: The vote was overwhelmingly in favor of the new law.
words.ex_cn: 投票压倒性地支持这项新法律。
words.en: In a way that is very great or very strong; so powerful that you cannot resist it or decide how to react.

words.tr: phrase. 达到（某数值）的峰值；在…达到最高点
words.ex: The temperature peaks at 30 degrees in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天温度最高达到30度。
words.en: To reach the highest point or level of something.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr: adj. 可以忽略的；
words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: phrase. 相比之下显得暗淡无光；不如……
words.ex: His performance paled in comparison to his brother's.
words.ex_cn: 他的表现与他哥哥相比相形见绌。
words.en: Seemed much less important or impressive when compared to something else.

words.tr: phrase. 被…遮蔽；被…掩盖；因…而黯然失色
words.ex: His talent was overshadowed by his brother's fame.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华被他哥哥的名气盖过了。
words.en: Was made less noticeable or important by the presence of something else.

words.tr: phrase. 相比之下；相反
words.ex: He likes cats. In contrast, she prefers dogs.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢猫。相比之下，她更喜欢狗。
words.en: used when you are comparing two things or people and saying that the second one is very different from the first

words.tr: phrase. 与此相反；正相反
words.ex: He says he likes quiet, on the contrary, he always listens to loud music.
words.ex_cn: 他说他喜欢安静，相反，他总是听大声的音乐。
words.en: You use 'on the contrary' when you are contradicting what has just been said or implied, or making a contrast between two things.

words.tr: adv. 同样地；平等地；
words.ex: They equally share the housework.
words.ex_cn: 他们同样分担家务。
words.en: In a manner that is the same in amount, degree, or value.

words.tr: phrase. 映照这个；反射这个；反映这个
words.ex: The lake was mirroring this beautiful sunset.
words.ex_cn: 湖面映照着这美丽的日落。
words.en: Reflecting or showing a similar pattern or trend to this.

words.tr: adv. 相似地；类似地；
words.ex: He likes apples, and similarly, his sister likes them too.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果，同样，他妹妹也喜欢。
words.en: in a similar way

words.tr: adv. 同样地；
words.ex: I like coffee, and she likes it likewise.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡，她也喜欢。
words.en: You use likewise when you are comparing two methods, states, or situations and saying that they are similar.

words.tr: adv. 类似地；相似地
words.ex: He solved the math problem, and analogously, she solved the science one.
words.ex_cn: 他解决了这道数学题，同样地，她解决了这道科学题。
words.en: In a similar or comparable way.

words.tr: adv. 与此同时；
words.ex: He was cooking dinner. Meanwhile, his daughter did her homework.
words.ex_cn: 他正在做晚饭，与此同时，他的女儿在做作业。
words.en: In the intervening period of time; at the same time.

words.tr: phrase. 其间；同时
words.ex: He is cooking dinner. In the meantime, she is setting the table.
words.ex_cn: 他正在做晚饭，与此同时，她正在摆桌子。
words.en: In the meantime is used to indicate that something else is happening or will happen while a particular event or situation is continuing.

words.tr: adv. 同时地
words.ex: He sings and plays guitar simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 他一边唱歌一边弹吉他。
words.en: If two or more things happen simultaneously, they happen at exactly the same time.

words.tr: phrase. 以后；后来；之后
words.ex: He ate breakfast, and after that, he went to school.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了早餐，之后去上学了。
words.en: Following a previous event or statement; subsequently.

words.tr: phrase. 从此时起；从此以后
words.ex: From this time onwards, he wakes up at 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 从现在开始，他早上六点起床。
words.en: From this point in time forward; starting now and continuing into the future.

words.tr: phrase. 从那时起；从此以后
words.ex: He started running every day from then onwards.
words.ex_cn: 从那时起，他每天开始跑步。
words.en: From that point in time forward; starting then and continuing into the future.

words.tr: phrase. 从那时起，从那以后
words.ex: He failed the test, but from then on he studied every day.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但从那以后他每天学习。
words.en: From a particular time in the past onwards.

words.tr: adv. 后来；然后；
words.ex: We had dinner, and afterwards we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 我们吃了晚饭，后来去散步了。
words.en: If you do something or if something happens afterwards, you do it or it happens after a particular event or time that has already been mentioned.

words.tr: phrase. 紧随其后的是；接着是；其后跟着
words.ex: It was followed by a loud clap of thunder.
words.ex_cn: 紧接着是一声巨响的雷声。
words.en: It was succeeded by; something happened after it.

words.tr: adv. 因此；
words.ex: He didn't study, consequently he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有学习，因此考试不及格。
words.en: As a result; therefore.

words.tr: phrase. 结果
words.ex: He didn't study hard, as a result, he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有努力学习，结果考试不及格。
words.en: used to introduce the consequence or effect of a particular situation or event

words.tr: adv. 因此；从而；
words.ex: He studied hard, thereby passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，因此通过了考试。
words.en: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.

words.tr: phrase. 导致；通向；引起
words.ex: He worked hard, leading to better grades.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，导致成绩提高了。
words.en: Leading to is used to indicate that one thing is a result of another or that one thing causes another.

words.tr: phrase. 而且；此外；再者
words.ex: I like reading books, and furthermore, I write my own stories.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢读书，而且我还写自己的故事。
words.en: In addition to what has already been mentioned; moreover.

words.tr: adv. 此外；
words.ex: He likes reading books; moreover, he writes his own stories.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读书；此外，他还写自己的故事。
words.en: You use moreover to introduce a piece of information that adds to or supports the previous statement.

words.tr: adv. 此外
words.ex: He likes math, and additionally, he enjoys science.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢数学，此外，他还喜欢科学。
words.en: You use additionally to introduce extra information or to emphasize a point.

words.tr: adv. 具体地；明确地；
words.ex: He explained the rules specifically.
words.ex_cn: 他具体地解释了规则。
words.en: You use specifically to emphasize that something is given special attention and considered separately from other things of the same kind.

words.tr: phrase. 尤其；特别
words.ex: I like fruits, in particular apples.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果。
words.en: Especially; more than other things or people.

words.tr: adv. 相反地
words.ex: He likes coffee; conversely, she prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡；相反，她更喜欢茶。
words.en: In a way that is the opposite or reverse of something else.

words.tr: conj. 然而；
words.ex: He likes coffee, whereas she prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡，然而她更喜欢茶。
words.en: You use whereas to introduce a comment which contrasts with what is said in the main clause.

words.tr: phrase. 比较起来
words.ex: He is slow, by comparison, his brother is fast.
words.ex_cn: 相比之下，他很慢，他弟弟很快。
words.en: When you say that something is true by comparison, you mean that it is true when compared to something else.

words.tr: phrase. 明显不同；显著差异
words.ex: The two results differ significantly.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果有显著差异。
words.en: To be significantly different in nature, form, or quality.

words.tr: phrase. 另一方面
words.ex: I like coffee, on the other hand, my brother prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡，另一方面，我弟弟更喜欢茶。
words.en: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously

words.tr: adv. 或者；作为一种选择；
words.ex: You can take the bus, or alternatively, walk to school.
words.ex_cn: 你可以坐公交车，或者 alternatively，走路去学校。
words.en: Used to introduce a suggestion that is different from the one already mentioned.

words.tr: adv. 同时发生地
words.ex: He works and studies concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 他同时工作和学习。
words.en: At the same time; simultaneously.
